answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, externally priced bond before it may submit work, with rewards and reputation accruing only after independent verification. If an agent cheats or its work fails, the bond is slashed; creating a hundred sybils therefore means tying up a hundred bonds, not merely generating names. This makes attacks costly in capital and exposes each identity to loss. A crystal-clear rule can prevent a yarrow of cheap accounts from making the audit hollow.
